title: Bosch Dishwasher E15 Error Code: How to Fix a Water Leak Fault
metaDescription: Bosch dishwasher showing E15 and won't run? It means the Aquastop leak sensor detected water in the base pan. Here's how to find the leak and reset it.
symptom: The display shows "E15", the dishwasher won't start a new cycle, and there may be visible water in the base of the unit.
partsNeeded: Replacement fill hose or drain hose (only if a hose is the source of the leak)

steps.heading: Understand what E15 means
steps.body: Bosch's Aquastop system has a float switch in the base pan that trips E15 the moment it detects standing water — it's a safety feature, not a random glitch, and it will keep blocking new cycles until the water is gone and the float resets.

steps.heading: Turn off water supply and power
steps.body: Shut off the water supply valve under the sink that feeds the dishwasher, and cut power at the breaker. This stops any active leak from continuing while you investigate.

steps.heading: Remove standing water from the base pan
steps.body: Pull the dishwasher out or open the front lower panel/kickplate to access the base. Soak up standing water with towels or a wet/dry vac — the float switch needs to see a genuinely dry pan to reset.

steps.heading: Trace the leak to its source
steps.body: With the base dry, run a short cycle while briefly watching from outside for where water reappears: the door gasket, the fill hose connections, the drain hose/pump gasket, and the tub-to-pump seal are the most common culprits.

steps.heading: Fix or replace the leaking component
steps.body: A worn door gasket or a loose hose clamp can often be reseated or replaced cheaply. If the leak traces to the pump/tub seal itself, that's a bigger job — note it and consider a professional at that point.

steps.heading: Dry the base pan fully and reset
steps.body: Once the leak source is addressed, thoroughly dry the base pan again, restore water and power, and start a normal cycle to confirm E15 doesn't return.

whenToCallAPro: If you can't find a visible leak source after drying and re-running the dishwasher, or if the leak traces to the tub seal or pump housing, call a professional — those repairs usually require partially disassembling the unit, and getting it wrong can turn a small leak into a bigger one.
safetyWarnings: Shut off both the water supply and the circuit breaker before reaching into the base pan — you'll have water and mains voltage in the same space.
Standing water plus a household electrical circuit is a shock hazard — never touch internal components while water is still present.
If the leak is significant or recurring, don't just keep resetting and running the dishwasher — repeated water exposure can damage the subfloor and cabinetry.
